translations.text: Since many have undertaken to write an account of the events that have been fully accomplished among us,
just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word,
it seemed good to me also, having followed everything from the first with all truthfulness, to write to you in order, most excellent God-loving Theophilus,
so that you may know the certainty of the words in which you have been instructed.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a certain priest named Zechariah, of the daily order of service of Abijah, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
And both of them were righteous before God, and they walked blameless in all the commandments of the righteousness of the Lord.
And they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both of them were advanced in their days.
And it happened, while he was serving as priest in the order of his daily service before God,
that according to the custom of the priesthood it fell to him by lot to burn incense, and he entered the temple of the Lord.
And the whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of the burning of incense.
And an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right of the altar of incense.
And Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
The angel said to him: Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayers have been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
And he will be joy and gladness to you, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great before the Lord, and he shall drink no wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb.
And he will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.

And he himself will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers toward the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready for the Lord a prepared people.
And Zechariah said to the angel: How shall I know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in her days.
The angel answered and said to him: I am Gabriel, who stand before the face of God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day that this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time.
And the people stood waiting for Zechariah, and they marveled at his delay in the temple.
And when he came out, he could not speak to them, and they understood that he had seen some vision in the temple; and he kept making signs to them and remained speechless.
And when the days of his service were completed, he went away to his house.
And after those days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she hid herself for five months, saying,
"Thus the Lord has done for me in these days, in which he looked upon me to take away my reproach among men."
And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city of Galilee whose name was Nazareth,
to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house and tribe of David; and the name of the virgin was Mary.
And the angel came in to her and said to her: "Rejoice, favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women."
But when she saw him, she was troubled at his word and pondered: "What kind of greeting is this?"
And the angel said to her: "Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found grace before God.
And behold, lo, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.
He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end."
Mary said to the angel: "How will this be for me, since I do not know a man?"

The angel answered and said to her: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the one who is born will also be called holy and Son of the Most High.
And behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman, she too has conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren.
For no word is impossible before God."
Mary said to him: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord: let it be to me according to your word!" And the angel departed from her.
And Mary arose in those days and went in haste into the hill country, to a city of Judah.
And she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
And it came to pass, when Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, that the child leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit
and cried out with a loud voice and said: "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For behold, lo, as soon as the sound of your greeting came to my ears, this child leaped for joy in my womb.
And blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of the things spoken to her by the Lord."
And Mary said: "My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
for he has looked upon the lowliness of his handmaid; for behold, lo, from now on all generations will call me blessed;
for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name,
and his mercy is from generation to generation upon those who fear him;
He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts;
he has brought down the mighty from their thrones and lifted up the lowly;
he has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty;
he has helped Israel, his servant, in remembrance of his mercy,
as he spoke to our father Abraham and to his descendants forever.
And Mary stayed with Elizabeth for three months and went back to her own house.
Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.
And her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.
And on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to call him by his father's name, Zechariah.
But his mother answered and said: No, he shall be called John.
And they said to her: There is no one among your relatives who is called by that name.
And they made signs to his father to find out what he wanted him to be named.
And he asked for a writing tablet and wrote, saying: His name is John. And they were all amazed at this.
And immediately his mouth and his tongue were opened, and he spoke and blessed God.
And great fear came on all who lived around them; and throughout all the hill country of Judea people were talking about all these things.
And all who heard these things kept them in their hearts and said: What then will this child be? And the hand of the Lord was with him.
And his father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit, and he prophesied and said:
Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked upon his people and brought about their redemption;
and he has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David his servant,
as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old:
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us;
to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,
the oath that he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that, delivered from the hands of our enemies, without fear
we might serve him in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give knowledge of salvation to his people through the forgiveness of their sins,
through the mercy of the compassion of our God, by which the Dayspring from on high has visited us,
to shine upon those who sit in darkness and in the shadows of death, and to guide our feet into the way of peace.
And the child grew and became strong in spirit. And he was in the wilderness until the day of his appearing to Israel.
And it came to pass in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered.
This was the first registration, during the governorship of Quirinius in Syria.
And all went to be registered, each one to his own city.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and lineage of David,
to be registered with Mary, who was betrothed to him, and she was with child.
And it came to pass, while they were still there, that the days of her giving birth were fulfilled.
And she bore her firstborn son, and she wrapped him in swaddling clothes and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
And there were shepherds in that same region, staying in the fields and keeping the night watch over their flock.
And behold, an angel of the Lord stood over them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were afraid with great fear.
And the angel of the Lord said to them: Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people:
for today there has been born to you a Savior, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.
And this will be a sign to you: you will find the child wrapped and lying in a manger.
And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the hosts of heaven, praising God and saying:
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, and among men goodwill.

And it came to pass, when the angels had gone up into heaven, that the shepherds said to one another: Let us go over as far as Bethlehem and see this word that has come to us, which the Lord has made known to us.
And they came quickly and found Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.
And when they saw, they understood the word that had been spoken to them about the child.
And all who heard marveled at the word that the shepherds spoke to them.
But Mary kept these words and laid them up in her heart.
And the shepherds turned back and went away, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.
And when the eight days of his circumcision were completed, they called his name Jesus, the name he had been given by the angel before he came to be in his mother's womb.
And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought the child up to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord,
as it is written in the law of the Lord: "Every male child that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord,"
and to give an offering, as it is said in the law of the Lord: "two turtledoves, or two young pigeons."
And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon; and this man was righteous and feared the Lord, and he was waiting for the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had seen the Lord's Anointed.
And he came by the Holy Spirit into the temple of the Lord. And when the child Jesus was brought in by his father and mother, so that they might do for him according to the custom of the law,
he took him in his arms and blessed God and said:
"Now, Master, let your servant depart in peace, according to your word,
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared before the face of all peoples,
a light to shine upon the Gentiles, and the glory of your people Israel."
And Joseph and his mother were amazed at the words spoken about him.
And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother: "Behold, this child is set for the fall and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that will be spoken against.
And a sword will pass through your own soul too, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed."
And there was Anna the prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was advanced in many days, and had lived with her husband seven years from her virginity.
And she was a widow of about eighty-four years, who did not depart from the temple, serving with fasting and prayer and worship night and day.
At that very hour she came up and gave thanks to God, and spoke about him to all who were waiting for redemption in Jerusalem.
And when they had done everything for him according to the law of the Lord, they returned and went to Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth.
And the child grew and became strong in spirit and was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
And his parents used to go up to Jerusalem every year for the feast of Passover.
And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem for the feast, as they were accustomed to do.
And when the days were completed and they were leaving, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and Joseph and his mother did not know it.
They supposed that he was with the travelling company. And they went a day's journey, and they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances,
and they did not find him. And they returned to Jerusalem and looked for him there.
And after three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
And they saw him and were astonished. His mother said to him: "Child, why have you done this to us? Look, your father and I are in distress [?] and are looking for you."
And he said to them: "Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be with my Father?"
And they did not understand the word that he said to them.
And he went with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart.
And Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature and in grace before God and people.

In the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip was tetrarch of Ituraea and the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
in the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of the Lord came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
And he went through all the region around the Jordan and preached a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
As it is written in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah, which says: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the ways of the Lord and make his paths straight.
Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall become straight, and the rough shall become a level road.
And all flesh shall see the salvation of God."
And he said to the crowds who went out to him to be baptized by him: "You offspring of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come?
So now bear fruit worthy of repentance, and do not think and say in your hearts, 'We have Abraham as our father.' I tell you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
For even now the axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree that does not bring forth good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."
And the crowds asked him, saying: "What then shall we do?"
He answered and said to them: "Whoever has two garments, let him give to the one who has none; and let him do likewise with food."
Tax collectors also came to him to be baptized, and they said to him: "Teacher, what shall we do?"
And he said to them: "Do nothing more than what has been appointed for you."
Those enlisted as soldiers also asked him, saying: "And what shall we do?" And he said to them: "Do not oppress anyone, do not accuse anyone falsely, and be content with your wages."
And as the people were waiting in expectation, and all were wondering in their hearts about John, whether perhaps he was the Christ,
John answered them all, saying: "I baptize you with water, but one mightier than I is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hands; he will clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire."
And with many other things as well he exhorted the people and proclaimed the good news to them.
But Herod, the ruler of the four principalities, because John rebuked him about Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, and about all the evil that Herod had done,
added this as well on top of all of it, and shut John up in prison.
And it happened that, when all the people were being baptised, Jesus too was baptised and was praying; and the heavens were opened,
and the Holy Spirit came down upon him in bodily form, like a dove; and a voice came from heaven and said: "You are my beloved Son; I am well pleased with you."
And Jesus himself was just about to reach his thirtieth year. He was, as people supposed, the son of Joseph, the son of Heli,
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah,
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
the son of Jose, the son of Eliezer, the son of Joram, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim,
the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,
the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, came back from the Jordan, and the Spirit led him into the wilderness.
And for forty days he was tempted by the devil, and he ate nothing during those days. And when those days were over, he was hungry.
And the devil said to him: "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
Jesus answered and said to him: "It is written: A person shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God."
And he took him up onto a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time,
And the devil said to him: I will give you authority over all this and its glory, for it has been given to me, and I give it to whomever I wish;
if you bow down in worship before me, all this will be yours.
Jesus answered and said to him: Get behind me, devil; it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve.
And he brought him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple and said to him: If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here to the ground,
for it is written: He has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you,
and they will lift you up on their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.
Jesus answered and said to him: It is said: You shall not tempt the Lord your God.
And when the devil had finished every temptation, he departed from him until an appointed time.
And Jesus returned in the power of the Holy Spirit to Galilee; and a report about him went out through all the surrounding region.
And he taught in their synagogues and was glorified by all.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and as was his custom he went into their synagogue on the Sabbath day.
And they gave him the book of the prophet Isaiah, and he stood up to read, and he opened the book and found the place where it was written:

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor; he has sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to the captives and sight to the blind, to set free those who are crushed,
and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.
And he closed the book, gave it to the attendant, and sat down; and the eyes of the whole assembly were fixed on him.
And he began to say to them: Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.
And all bore witness to him and marveled at the words of grace that came out of his mouth, and they said: Is this not the son of Joseph?
And he said to them: Surely you will say to me this proverb: Physician, heal yourself! And they said to him: All the things we have heard were done in Capernaum, do here too, in your own homeland!
But he said to them: Amen, I say to you, no prophet is accepted in his own homeland.
But truly I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months, when there was a great famine over all the land.
And Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to a widow woman at Zarephath of Sidon.
And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.
And all who were in the synagogue were filled with anger when they heard this.
And they rose up and drove him out of the city and brought him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, in order to throw him down.
But he passed through their midst and went away.
And he went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and he was teaching them on the Sabbath.
And they were amazed at his teaching, because his word was with authority.
And in their synagogue there was a man who had an unclean spirit, and he cried out with a loud voice:
"Ah, what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? You have come to destroy us. I know who you are: the Holy One of God."
And Jesus rebuked him and said to him, "Be silent, and come out of him!" And the demon threw him down in their midst and came out of him, and did him no harm.
And amazement came upon them all, and they were discussing with one another and saying, "What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out."
And the report about him was spreading through all the places of the surrounding countryside.
And he rose and left the synagogue and entered the house of Simon. Now Simon's mother-in-law was gripped by a high fever, and they told him about her.
And he stood over her and rebuked the fever. And immediately it left her, and she rose and was serving them.
And just as the sun was setting, all who had people sick with various kinds of diseases brought them to him. And he laid his hand on each one of them and healed them.
And demons were coming out of many, crying out and saying, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God!" And he did not allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.

And when it was day, he went out from there and went away to a deserted place. And the people were looking for him, and they came to him and were trying to hold him back, so that he would not go away from them.
But he said to them, "I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also, for that is why I was sent."
And he was preaching in all the synagogues of Galilee.
And it happened, as the crowd was pressing upon him to hear the word of God, that he was standing by the shore of the lake of Gennesaret.
And he saw two boats standing at the shore of the lake; but the fishermen had gotten out of the boats and were washing their nets.
And he got into one of the boats, which was Simon's, and told them to put out a little from the land. And he sat down and was teaching the crowd from the boat.
And when he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "Put out into the deep and let down your net for a catch."
Simon answered and said to him, "Master, we toiled all night and caught nothing, but at your word let us let down the net."
And when they had done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets were breaking.
And they signaled to those who were in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they were sinking.
And when Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees and said to him, "Go away from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord."
For amazement had seized him and all who were with him at the catch of fish which they had taken.
And so also James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon's partners. And Jesus said to Simon, "Do not be afraid, Simon! From now on you will be a fisher of men."
And they brought the boat to land, left everything, and followed him.

And it happened, when he entered one of the cities, that behold, there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, saying to him: "Lord, if you are willing, you are able to heal me."
And he stretched out his hand, touched him and said to him: "I am willing; be cleansed!" And immediately the leprosy left him.
And he himself commanded him to tell no one, but: "Go and show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
And the word about him spread all the more, and great crowds gathered to hear and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
But he himself would withdraw into the wilderness and pray.

And it happened on one day that Jesus himself was teaching them. And there were sitting there Pharisees and teachers of the law who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem, and the power of God was present for healing them.
And behold, men were bringing on a bed a man who was paralysed, and they wanted to bring him in and set him before him.
And they could not find a way to bring him in because of the crowd. They went up onto the roof, removed the tiles, and let the man down with the bed in front of Jesus.
And when he saw their faith, he said to him: "Man, your sins are forgiven you!"
And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying: "Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who has the power to forgive sins, except God alone?"
Jesus perceived their thoughts, answered and said to them: "Why are you reasoning this in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — he said to the paralysed man: "I say to you, get up, take up your bed and go to your home!"
And immediately he got up before them, took up the bed on which he had been lying, and went to his home glorifying God.
Amazement seized them all, and they glorified God. And fear fell upon them, and they said: "We have seen a most glorious glory today."
And after this he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him: "Follow me!"
And he left everything, got up and followed him.
And Levi prepared a great feast for Jesus in his house, and there was a large gathering of tax collectors and others who were reclining at table with them.
And the Pharisees and their scribes grumbled to his disciples, saying: "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are in grievous sickness do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, so that they may repent."
But they said to him: "Why do John's disciples fast often and make supplications, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but your disciples eat and drink?"
But Jesus said to them: "Can the sons of the bridegroom be made to fast while the bridegroom is with them?
But the days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast in those days."
And he also spoke to them in a parable: No one puts a patch from a new garment on an old garment, lest he tear the new one as well; and the patch from the new garment does not match the old one.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins, lest the new wine burst the wineskins, and the wine be spilled, and the wineskins be ruined;
but new wine must be poured into new wineskins, and both are preserved.
And no one who has drunk old wine immediately wants new, for he says: The old is better.
And it happened on the second sabbath that he was going through a sown field. And his disciples were plucking heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands, and eating.
But some of the Pharisees said to them: Why are you doing on the sabbath what is not lawful?
Jesus answered and said to them: Have you not even read this, what David did when he and those with him were hungry,
how he went into the house of God and ate the bread of offering, and gave some also to those with him, which it is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests alone?
And he said to them: The Son of Man is lord of the sabbath also.
And it happened on another sabbath also that he went into their synagogue and was teaching them. And there was a man there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and Pharisees were watching him to see whether he would heal on the sabbath, so that they might find a way to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts, and he said to the man whose hand was withered: Get up and come forward into the middle! And he got up and stood in the middle.
And Jesus said to them: I will ask you something: What is lawful on the sabbath, to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to kill?
And he looked around at them all and said to the man: Stretch out your hand! And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored like the other.
But they were filled with malice and were plotting with one another what they might do to Jesus.
And it happened in those days that he went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the night in prayer to God.
And when day dawned, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, whom he named Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, and James son of Alphaeus, and Simon, who was called the Zealot,
and Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became the betrayer.
And he came down with them and stood on a level place, with the crowd of his disciples and a very great multitude of other people from Judea and Jerusalem and from the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon,
who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases; and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
And the whole crowd was trying to come near him, for power went out from him and healed them all.
And he lifted up his eyes toward his disciples and said: Blessed are you who are poor in spirit, for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they cast you out and revile you and reject your name as evil, for the sake of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and be glad, for behold, your reward is great in heaven; for their fathers did the same to the prophets.
But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation.
Woe to you who are full now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when people speak well of you, for their fathers did the same to the false prophets.
But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, and do good to those who hate you.
Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
Whoever strikes you on the cheek, offer him the other side as well; and whoever takes your garment from you, do not withhold your tunic either.
Give to everyone who asks of you; and whoever takes from you, do not demand it back.
And just as you want people to do to you, do the same to them likewise.
And if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do this.
And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive back, what credit is that to you? For even sinners lend to sinners, so that they may receive the same amount back.

But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, despairing of nothing; and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for he himself is kind even to the ungrateful and the wicked.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged; do not condemn, and you will not be condemned; forgive, and you will be forgiven.

Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, filled up, and running over, will they give into your bosom; for by the same measure with which you measure out, it will be measured back to you.
He also told them a parable: Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not greater than his teacher; but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye, and do not notice the beam in your own eye?

Or how can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,' when you yourself do not see the beam in your own eye? Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
For there is no good tree that bears bad fruit, nor again a bad tree that produces good fruit.
For each tree is known by its own fruit; for figs are not gathered from thorns, nor are grapes harvested from brambles.
The good man brings forth good out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings forth evil out of the evil treasure of his heart; for out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks.
Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and do not do what I tell you?
Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you whom he is like.

He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid the foundation on the rock; and when there was a flood, the river struck that house and could not shake it, for it had been founded on the rock.
But the one who has heard and does not do is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation; the river struck it, and at once it fell; and the fall of that house was great.
And when Jesus had finished these words in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum.
And a certain centurion's servant, who was dear to him, was sick and close to death.
And he heard about Jesus and sent elders of the Jews to him to entreat him to come and heal his servant.
And those who came to Jesus besought him earnestly and said to him: "He is worthy that you should do this for him,
for he loves our nation, and he built the synagogue for us."

And Jesus went with them. And when he had come near the house, the centurion sent friends to him and said: "Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy that you should come in under the roof of my house;
for which reason I did not even consider myself worthy to come to you. But only say it with a word, and this servant of mine will be healed.
For I too am a man set under authority, and I have soldiers under me; and I say to this one, 'Go!' and he goes; and to another, 'Come!' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this!' and he does it."
And when Jesus heard this, he marveled at his faith, and he turned to the crowd and said: "Truly I say to you, not even in Israel have I found such faith."
And those who had been sent returned to his house and found his servant alive.
And after this it came to pass that he was going to a city called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd were going with him.
And as he drew near to the gate of the city, behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only-begotten son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a large crowd from that city was with her.
And Jesus saw that woman and had compassion on her and said to her: "Do not weep!"
And he came up to the bier and touched it, and those who were carrying the bier stood still. And he said to him: "Young man, I say to you, arise!"
And the dead man sat up and began to speak; and he gave him to his mother.
And fear fell upon them all, and they glorified God and said: "A great prophet has arisen among us," and "God has visited his people."
And this report about him spread through all Judea and all the surrounding region.
And his disciples told John about all these things.
And John called two of his disciples and sent them to Jesus and said: "Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?"
And when the men came to him, they said: "John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying: 'Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?'"
In that hour he healed many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and to many who were blind he granted sight.

And Jesus answered and said to them: "Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is proclaimed to the poor.
And blessed is he who does not stumble because of me."
And when John's messengers had gone away, Jesus began to speak to the people about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are in glorious and luxurious clothing are in royal palaces.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
For this is the one of whom it is written: 'Behold, I will send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your ways before you.'
For I tell you: among those born of women there is no prophet greater than John the Baptist, yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."
And all the people who heard, and the tax collectors, justified God, having been baptized with the baptism of John.
But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law rejected the purpose of God for themselves, for they had not been baptized by him.
"To whom shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?
They are like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call out to their companions and say: 'We piped for you, and you did not dance; we wailed for you, and you did not weep.'
For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say: 'He has a demon.'
The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say: 'Look, a glutton and a drinker of wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.'
And wisdom is justified by all her children."
One of the Pharisees asked him to eat bread with him; and he went into the Pharisee's house and sat down at table.
And there was a woman in that city who was a sinner. She heard that he was in the Pharisee's house, and she brought an alabaster jar of ointment.
And she stood at his feet weeping, and began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with the hair of her head, and kissed his feet and anointed them with the ointment.
When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said in his heart: "If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what sort of woman this is who is touching him, for she is a sinner."
Jesus answered and said to him: "Simon, I have something to say to you." And he said: "Teacher, speak!"
And he said: "A certain moneylender had two debtors: one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
And since they had nothing, he forgave them both. Now tell me: which of them will love him more?"
Simon answered and said: "I suppose the one to whom he forgave more." And he said: "You have judged rightly."
And he turned to the woman and said to Simon: "Do you see this woman? I came into your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair;
you gave me no kiss, but she, from the time she came in, has not ceased kissing my feet;
you did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment,
For this reason I tell you: her many sins are forgiven her, because she loved much. But the one to whom little is forgiven loves little.
And he said to her, "Your sins are forgiven you!"
And those who were reclining at table with him began to say in their hearts, "Who is this, who forgives sins?"
He said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go in peace!"
And after this he went from city to city and from village to village, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God; and the twelve disciples were with him,
and certain women who had been healed of unclean spirits and infirmities: Mary, who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, who served him from their own possessions.
And to those who were with him, the many crowds, and those who came to him from city after city, he spoke in a parable:
"A sower went out to sow his seed; and as he sowed, some fell on the road and was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it.
And other seed fell on rock; it sprang up and withered, because there was no depth of soil.
And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up and choked it.
And other seed fell on good ground, and it sprang up and bore fruit a hundredfold." As he said this, he called out: "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear."
His disciples asked him, "What is this parable?"
And he said to them, "To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to others it is given in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
Now this is the parable: the seed is the word of God.
Those on the road are those who hear; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, so that they may not believe and be saved.
And those on the rock are those who, when they hear, receive the word with joy, but these have no root; they believe for a time, and in the time of testing they fall away.
And what fell among the thorns, these are those who hear the word, and as they go on their way, they are choked by cares and riches and the pleasures of the world, and they do not become fruitful.
And what was sown on the good ground, these are those who hear the word with a good and kindly heart, and keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed; rather, one puts it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor any secret that will not be known and come out into the open.
See, then, how you listen: whoever has, to him more will be given; and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him."
His mother and his brothers came to him, and they could not reach him because of the crowd.
They told him, saying, "Your mother and your brothers are standing outside and wish to see you."
But he said to them, "My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it."
One day he got into a boat with his disciples, and he said to them, "Let us go across to the other side of the lake." And they set out.
As they were sailing, he fell asleep. A storm of wind came down on the lake, and the boat was filling with water, and they were in danger.
They came and woke him, saying, "Master, Master, we are perishing!" He got up and rebuked the wind and the raging of the waters; they ceased, and there was a great calm.
He said to them, "Where is your faith?" They were afraid and amazed, and said to one another, "Who then is this, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?"
And they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
As they stepped out onto land, a man from the city met him, who had demons in him. For a long time he had worn no clothes, and he did not live in a house but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down at his feet, and said in a loud voice, "What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I beg you, do not torment me."

For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him; they would bind him with chains and fetters and guard him, but he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon into the wilderness.
Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" He said, "Legion," because many demons had entered him.
And they begged him not to command them to go down into the abyss.
A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside, and they begged him to let them enter those pigs. And he gave them leave.
The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
When the herdsmen saw what had happened, they ran off and went and told it in the city and in the villages.
People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.
For those who had seen it told them how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
Then the whole crowd from the surrounding country of the Gadarenes begged him to leave them, for they were seized with great fear. So he got into the boat and went back again.
The man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might be with him. But he sent him away, saying,
"Return to your home and tell how much God has done for you." And he went away through all the city, proclaiming how much Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him there, for they were all waiting for him.
And behold, a man came whose name was Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to his house,
for he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. As he went, the crowds pressed around him.
There was a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians, and no one had been able to heal her.
She came up from behind and touched the fringe of his garment, and at once her flow of blood stopped.
And Jesus said, "Who touched me?" When they all denied it, Peter and those with him said to him, "Master, the crowds surround you and press in on you, and you say, 'Who touched me?'"
But Jesus said to him, "Someone touched me, for I perceived power going out from me."

When the woman saw that she had not remained hidden, she came trembling and fell down before him. In front of all the people she told him the reason she had touched him, and how she had been healed at once.
And Jesus said to her, "Do not be afraid, daughter. Your faith has saved you. Go in peace!"
While he was still speaking, someone came from the house of the ruler of the synagogue and said to him, "Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the Teacher."
But when Jesus heard this, he said to him, "Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be saved."
When Jesus came to the house, he let no one go in with him except Peter, James and John, and the girl's father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said to them, "Do not weep, for the girl is not dead but asleep."
And they laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
But he put them all out, took the girl by the hand, and called out to her, "Child, arise!"
And her spirit returned, and she got up at once. And he ordered that she be given something to eat.
Her father and mother were amazed. But he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.
Jesus called his twelve disciples together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to heal diseases.
And he sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
And he said to them, "Take nothing for the journey: no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, and do not have two garments.
Whatever house you enter, stay there, and leave from there.
And wherever they do not receive you, when you leave that town, shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them."
So they went out and travelled through the villages, preaching the good news and healing the sick everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard about all the things that were being done by him, and he was perplexed, because some were saying, "John the Baptist has risen from the dead."
Others were saying, "Elijah has appeared," and still others, "One of the prophets of old has risen."
But Herod said, "I beheaded John. But who is this about whom I hear such things? I do not know." And he wanted to see him.
The apostles returned and told Jesus everything they had done. And he took them with him and withdrew privately to a deserted place belonging to a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowds learned of it and followed him. He received them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and he healed those who needed healing.

As the day began to decline, the Twelve came and said to him, "Send this crowd away, so that they may go to the surrounding villages and farms, lodge there, and find food for themselves, because we are here in a deserted place."
But Jesus said to them, "You give them something to eat." And they said, "We have nothing more than five loaves of barley bread and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all these people."
For the men were about five thousand. Jesus said to his disciples, "Make these men sit down in groups for eating, fifty in each."
And they did so, and made all the people sit down.
And he himself took the five loaves and the two fish, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and blessed them, and broke them, and kept giving them to the disciples to set before the people.
And they all ate and were filled; and they took up what was left over to them of the broken pieces, twelve baskets.
And it happened, as he was praying by himself, that the disciples were with him. He asked them and said, "Who do these people think I am, and what do they say I am?"
And they answered and said to him, "John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and some say that one of the prophets of old has risen."
And Jesus said to them, "But who do you think I am?" Peter answered and said to him, "The Anointed One of God."
And he sternly warned them, and commanded them to tell this to no one.
And he said to them, "The Son of Man must suffer much, and be treated with contempt by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and on the third day rise again."
And he said to all, "Whoever wishes to follow me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me."
"For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it."
"What profit is it to a man if he gains the whole world and loses himself, or suffers loss?"
"Whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of Man too will be ashamed when he comes in his own glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels."
"I tell you: there are some of those standing here who will not see the taste of death until they see the kingdom of God."
And it happened about eight days after these words that Jesus took Peter and James and John and went up the mountain to pray.
And it happened, as he was praying, that the appearance of his face became different, and his clothing became white and shining.
And behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
who appeared in glory and were speaking of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.
But Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep; and when they woke up, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

And it happened, as they were parting from him, that Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tents here: one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah" — for he did not know what he was saying.
And as he was saying this, behold, a cloud overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
And a voice came out of the cloud: "This is my beloved Son; listen to him!"
And when this voice had come, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent and in those days told no one anything of what they had seen.
And it happened on the next day, as they came down from the mountain, that a great crowd came to meet him.
And behold, a man from the crowd cried out and said: Teacher, I beg you, look upon my son, for he is my only child.
And an evil spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it throws him into convulsions, and he foams [?], and it departs from him with difficulty and crushes him.
And I begged your disciples to drive it out, and they could not.
But Jesus answered and said to him: O unbelieving and perverse generation! How long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here to me!
And while he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him. Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy and gave him back to his father.
And all were astonished at the majesty of God, and all were amazed at everything that Jesus was doing. And Jesus said to his disciples:
Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of men.
But they did not understand this saying, and it was hidden from them so that they could not grasp it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
A thought also entered their minds: which of them would be the greatest?
But Jesus knew the thoughts of their hearts, and he brought a child and stood him before them,
and said to them: Whoever receives this child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For the one who is least among you all, he is great.
John answered and said: Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow along with us.
Jesus said to him: Do not stop him, for whoever is not our enemy is on our side.
And it came to pass, when the days of his ascension were being fulfilled, that he himself set his face to go up to Jerusalem.
And he sent messengers ahead of him. And they went and entered a village of the Samaritans, to make preparations for him.
And they did not receive them, because his face was set toward going to Jerusalem.
When his disciples James and John saw this, they said: Lord, do you want us to speak, so that fire may come down from heaven and destroy them, as Elijah did?
Jesus turned and rebuked them and said: Do you not know of what spirit you are?
For the Son of Man did not come to destroy people's lives, but to save them. And they went on to another village.
And it came to pass, as they were going along the road, that someone said to him: I will follow you wherever you go.
Jesus said to him: Foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have dwellings, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.
And to another he said: Follow me! And he said: Lord, let me first go and bury my father.
Jesus said to him: Let the dead bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim far and wide the kingdom of God.
Another said to him: I too will follow you, Lord, but first let me take leave of those in my household.
Jesus said to him: No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.
After this the Lord chose seventy others and sent them two by two ahead of him into every town and village where he was about to go.
And he said to them: "The harvest is great, but the workers are few. So pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
Go! Behold, I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Do not carry a purse, or a bag, or sandals for your feet, and do not greet anyone on the road.
Whatever house you enter, first say: 'Peace be to this house!'
If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
Stay in that same house, eating and drinking with them, for the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not go from house to house.
Whatever town you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you,
and heal the sick in it, and say to them: 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'
But whatever town you enter and they do not receive you, as you go out into its streets, say to them:
'Behold, even the dust of your town that has clung to our feet we shake off against you. Yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near.'
I tell you, on that day it will be more bearable for the people of Sodom than for that town.
Woe to you, Chorazin, and woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, do not be exalted up to heaven; rather, you will go down to hell.
Whoever listens to you listens to me; whoever rejects you rejects me; and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me."
The seventy returned with joy and said: "Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name."
Jesus said to them: "I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning.
Behold, I give you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.
But do not rejoice in this, that the evil spirits submit to you; rather rejoice that your names have been written in heaven."

At that hour Jesus rejoiced in the Spirit and said: "I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this is what pleased you."

And he turned to the disciples and said: "All things have been given to me by my Father. No one knows who the Father is except the Son, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him."
Then he turned to his disciples privately and said: "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see, and the ears that hear what you hear.
For I tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it."
And behold, an expert in the law stood up to test Jesus, and said to him: "Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
And he said to him: "How is it written in the Law? How do you read it?"
And he said to him: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbour as yourself."
Jesus said to him: "You have answered rightly. Do this, and you will live."
But he wanted to justify himself, and he said to Jesus: "And who is my neighbour?"
Jesus answered and said to him: "A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and robbers fell upon him. They stripped him, wounded him, and went away, leaving him half-dead."
"Now by chance a certain priest was going down that same road, and he saw him and passed by."
"And likewise a Levite came to the same place, and he saw him and passed by."
"Then a certain Samaritan was travelling; he came to the same place, saw him, and had pity on him."
"And he came to him and bound up his wound, and poured on oil and wine, and set him on his own mount, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him."
"And on the next day, as he was leaving, he gave two denarii to the innkeeper and said to him: 'Take care of him, and if you spend anything more, when I come back I will repay you.'"
"Which of these three, then, do you think was a neighbour to the man who fell among the robbers?"
And he said: "The one who showed mercy to him." Jesus said to him: "Go, and you also do likewise."
And it happened, as they went on their way, that he entered a certain village. And there was a certain woman there whose name was Martha, and she received him into her house.
And she had a sister called Mary, who sat at Jesus' feet and listened to his words.
But Martha was busy and distracted with much serving. She came up and said to him: "Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me."
Jesus answered and said to her: "Martha, Martha! You are anxious and troubled about many things;
here one thing is needful. Mary has chosen the good portion, which will never be taken away from her."
And it happened that he was praying in a certain place. And when he had finished praying, one of his disciples said to him: "Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples."
And he said to them: "When you pray, say: Our Father, who are in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.
Give us our daily bread day by day.
And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive all who are indebted to us; and do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil."
And he said to them: "Which of you has a friend, and goes to him at midnight and says to him: 'Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him';
and he answers from within and says: 'Do not trouble me; the door is shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot get up and give it to you.'
I tell you, even if he cannot get up and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will get up and give him as much as he needs."
And I say to you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
Which father among you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
If you, then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.
And he cast out a demon from a certain man; the demon was mute. And when the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and all the people marveled.
But some of them said: "He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of demons."
And others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
But he knew their thoughts and said to them: "Every kingdom that is divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.
And if Satan is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say of me that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
If I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they themselves will be your judges.
If I cast out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own court, his possessions are in peace.
But when one stronger than he comes upon him and overcomes him, he takes away his armor in which he trusted and divides his spoils.
Whoever is not with me is my enemy, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
When an unclean spirit goes out of a person, it wanders through waterless places seeking rest, and finding none, it says: 'I will return to my house from which I came.'
And when it comes, it finds it swept and adorned.
Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and dwell in it, and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first."
And while he was still saying this, a certain woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him: "Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts that you sucked."
But he said: "Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it."
And as the crowd was gathering, he began to say to them: "This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will the Son of Man be to this generation.

The queen of the south will rise up at the judgment with the people of this generation and condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place or under a bushel, but on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
The lamp of the body is the eye. When your eye is sound, your whole body is full of light. But if your eye is evil, your whole body is full of darkness.
See to it, then, that the light in you is not darkness.
If your whole body is full of light and has no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when a lamp gives you light with its bright shining.
And as he was saying this, a certain Pharisee asked him to eat bread with him; and he went in and sat down.
And when the Pharisee saw it, he was astonished that he had not first washed before the meal.
The Lord said to him: "Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.
Hypocrites, did not he who made the outside make the inside as well?
But give what is fitting as alms, and see, everything of yours is clean.
But woe to you, Pharisees, for you take a tithe of mint and rue and every herb, and pass over justice and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without leaving the others undone.
Woe to you, hypocritical Pharisees, for you love the chief seats in the synagogues and greetings in the streets.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you are like unseen graves, and people walk over them without knowing it."
One of the lawyers answered and said to him: "Teacher, in saying this you insult us too."
And he said to him: "Woe to you lawyers also, for you load people with burdens hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the burden with even one finger.
Woe to you, for you build the tombs of the prophets, but your fathers killed them.
So you bear witness and approve the deeds of your fathers, for they killed them, and you build their tombs.
For this reason the Wisdom of God also said: 'I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,'
so that the blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the temple. Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
Woe to you, teachers of the law, for you have hidden the keys of knowledge; you yourselves do not enter, and you hinder those who are entering."
And as he was saying this to them in front of all the people, the scribes and the Pharisees began to plot evil, and his word was hard for them to bear, and they reviled him because of his many words.
And they watched him, to catch some word from his mouth, so that they might accuse him.

Meanwhile, when a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another, he began to speak first to his disciples, and said to them: "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
There is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
Therefore what you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have spoken in the ear in inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
And I tell you, my friends: do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more that they can do to you.
But I will show you whom you should fear: fear him who, after killing, has power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
Are not five sparrows sold for two assaria? And not one of them is hidden before God.
But even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not be afraid, then, for you are better than many sparrows.
And I tell you: everyone who confesses me before men, the Son of Man too will confess him before the angels of God.
And whoever denies me before men, he too will be denied before the angels of God.
And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but the one who blasphemes the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
And when they bring you into the synagogues and before rulers and authorities, do not be anxious about how or with what word you should answer, or what you should say,
for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that hour what you should say.
Someone from the crowd said to him: Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.
But he said to him: Man, who appointed me judge and divider over you?
And he said to them: Take heed and guard yourselves from all covetousness, for a person's life does not come from the abundance of his possessions.
And he also told them a parable, saying to them: The land of a certain rich man was fruitful.
And he reasoned in his heart and said: What shall I do, for I have nowhere to gather my produce?
And he said: This is what I will do: I will tear down my storehouses and build greater ones, and there I will gather all my produce and my goods.
And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many goods stored up for many years; take your rest, eat and drink, and be merry.
God said to him: Fool, this night your soul will be taken from you; and what you have prepared, whose will it be?
So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not made rich by God.
And Jesus said to his disciples: Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor for your body, what you will put on.
For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have no storehouse or place to gather into, and God feeds them. How much better are you than the birds?
Which of you, then, by being anxious can add one cubit to his stature?
If you are not able to do even the least thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin. But I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
If God so clothes what is in the field, which today is grass and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith?
And you, do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not indulge yourselves,
For the nations of the world seek all these things, but your Father knows what you need of all these.
But seek the kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father in heaven has been pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give alms, and make for yourselves wealth that does not grow old, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning.
And be like those men who are waiting for their lord, for when he will come back from the wedding, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.
Blessed are those servants whose lord comes and finds them awake. Amen, I tell you, he will gird himself and seat them at table, and he will come and stand before them and serve them.
And even if he comes in the second watch or the third and finds them so, blessed are they.
But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.
You also must be ready, for the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
Peter said to him, "Lord, are you telling this parable to us only, or to all the others too?"
And Jesus said, "Who then is the faithful and wise steward whom the lord will set over his servants to give them their wheat at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whose lord comes and finds him doing so.
Amen, I tell you, he will set him over all his possessions.
But if that servant says in his heart, 'My lord is delaying his coming,' and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
the lord of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign him his portion with the unbelievers.
And the servant who knows his lord's will and does not prepare himself according to his will shall be punished severely.

But the one who does not know, and does something deserving of punishment, will be beaten lightly. For of everyone to whom much was given, much will be required of him, and from the one to whom much was given, they will demand all the more.
I came to cast fire upon the earth, and what do I wish but that it were already kindled!
But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
Do you suppose that I came to bring peace upon the earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.
For from now on five in one house will be divided: three against two and two against three.
They will be divided, father from son and son from father, mother from daughter and daughter from mother, mother-in-law from her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law from mother-in-law."
Jesus also said to the crowd, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say at once, 'It is bringing rain,' and so it happens.
And when the south wind blows, you say, “There will be heat,” and so it is.
Hypocrites! You know how to judge the face of the earth and of the sky, so why do you not judge this present time?
And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

For when you are going with your opponent before the ruler, make an effort on the way to be released from him. Otherwise he may drag you to the judge, and the judge will hand you over to the officer, and the officer will throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid the very last small coin.
At that very time some people came and told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Jesus answered and said to them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered this?
I tell you, no. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower in Siloam fell on them: do you think that they were more guilty than all the other people who live in Jerusalem?
I tell you, no. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
And he told them this parable: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it and found none.
And he said to the vinedresser, ‘Look, for three years now I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree and have found none. Cut it down. Why should it even take up the ground for nothing?’
But he answered and said, ‘Lord, leave it this year as well, until I dig around it and put manure on it.
Perhaps it will bear fruit. If not, then you can cut it down.’”
And Jesus was teaching them in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said to her, “Woman, you are set free from your infirmity.”
And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight, and she walked and glorified God.

But the leader of the synagogue, angry that Jesus had healed her on the sabbath, answered and said to the people, “There are six days on which it is right to work. Come on those days and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.”
Jesus answered him and said, “Hypocrite! Does not each of you on the sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away and give it water?
And this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen years now, should she not have been set free from her bonds on the sabbath day?”
And as he said this, all his opponents were put to shame. And all the people rejoiced at all the glorious things that were being done by him.
And he said, “What shall I compare the kingdom of God to, and what is it like?
It is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his garden. It grew and became a great tree, and the birds of the sky made their home in its branches.”
And again he said, “What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?
I will liken it to leaven, which a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened.
And he went about through towns and villages, teaching, as he journeyed toward Jerusalem.
And someone said to him: "Lord, are those who are saved few?" And he said to them:
"Strive to enter through the narrow gate. For I tell you: many will seek to enter and will not be able.

Once the master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you stand outside and begin to knock at the door, saying, 'Lord, Lord, open to us!', he will answer and say to you: 'I do not know you, or who you are.'
Then you will begin to say: 'We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught us in our streets.'
And he will say to you: 'I do not know who you are. Depart from me, all you workers of lawlessness!'
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and yourselves cast outside.
And people will come from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south, and will sit at table in the kingdom of God.
And behold, there are some last who were first, and there are some first who were last."
On that day some Pharisees came to Jesus and said to him: "Get out and go away from here, for Herod wants to kill you."
But he answered and said to them: "Go and tell that fox: 'Behold, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will be finished.'
For I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the day after, because it cannot be that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you! How often I have wanted to gather your children together, as a bird gathers its own chicks under its wings, and you were not willing!
Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you: you will not see me from now on until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
And it happened that when Jesus went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on the Sabbath day to eat bread, they were watching him closely.
And behold, there was a man in front of him who was suffering from dropsy.
Jesus answered and said to the teachers of the Law and the Pharisees: "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?"
But they were silent. And he brought the man forward, healed him, and sent him away.
And he said to them: "Which of you, if his son or his ox falls into a pit, will not pull him out at once on the Sabbath day?"
And they could give him no answer to this.
And he told a parable to those who were invited, teaching them, as he noticed how they were choosing the places of honour at the table, and he said to them:
"When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not sit down in the first place at table, in case someone more honoured than you has been invited by him,
and the one who invited both you and him comes and says to you, 'Give your place to this man!' Then you will begin, in shame, to take the last place.
