But when someone invites you, go and sit down in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, move up higher!' Then you will have honour in front of all who sit at table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

He also said to the one who had invited him: When you give a midday meal or a supper, do not invite your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor rich neighbours, lest they in turn invite you, and it become a repayment to you.
But when you give a meal, invite the poor, the ignorant [?], the lame and the blind,
and you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you, and you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.
One of those reclining at table with him heard this and said to him: Blessed is he who will eat bread in the kingdom of God!
But he said to him: A certain man gave a great feast and invited many.
And at the hour of the feast he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited to come, for: Behold, my feast is all ready.
And every one of them, one by one, began to excuse himself. The first said to him: I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it. I beg you, release me; let me be excused.
And another said: I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. I beg you, let me be excused.
And then another said to him: I have married a wife, and because of her I cannot come.

And the servant came and told this to his master. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his servant: Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor and the strangers and the blind and the lame.
And the servant said: Lord, your command has been carried out, and there is still room.
And the master said to the servant: Go out onto the roads and the hedges, and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.
But I tell you: none of those men will taste this supper of mine, for many are called, but few are chosen.
And a great crowd was gathering to him; he turned and said to them:
Whoever comes to me and does not hate his father and his mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and furthermore even his own soul, cannot be my disciple.
And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate how much he will spend, whether he has enough to carry it through to completion?
Otherwise he may lay a foundation and be unable to finish it, and all who see it will begin to mock him
and say: This man began to build and was unable to finish.
Or what king, going to fight against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
If not, while the other is still far off, he sends an envoy and greets him in peace.
So also, every one of you who does not part from all his possessions cannot be my disciple.
Salt is good. But if the salt loses its savour, with what will it be salted?
It is of use neither for the soil nor for the dung heap; instead they throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to listen to him.
And the Pharisees and the scribes grumbled and said, "This man receives sinners and eats and drinks with them."
And he told them this parable, saying:
"Which man among you who has a hundred sheep and loses one of them does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it?
And when he finds it, he puts it on his shoulders with joy;
and when he comes to his house, he calls together his friends and neighbors and says to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.'
I tell you, in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over the ninety-nine righteous who have no need of repentance.
Or what woman who has ten drachmas and loses one does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search diligently until she finds it?
And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors and says to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that I lost.'
I tell you, in the same way there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
Then he went on and said: "A certain man had two sons.
And the younger one said to his father, 'Father, give me the share of the inheritance that falls to me.' And he divided his livelihood between them.
And not many days later the younger son gathered everything together and went away to a distant country, and there he squandered his substance, for he lived in impurity.
And when he had spent everything he had, a severe famine came over that country, and he began to be in want.
And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
And his heart longed to fill his belly with the carob pods that the pigs were eating, and no one gave him anything.
And when he came to himself, he said, 'How many of my father's hired servants have more than enough bread, and here I am perishing with hunger!
I will get up and go to my father and say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you,
and I am no longer worthy to be called your son; but make me like one of your laborers."'
And he got up and came to his father. And while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion. And he ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
And the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'
His father said to his servants, 'Bring out the first robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet!
And bring the fattened calf and kill it, and let us eat and rejoice,
for this son of mine was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.' And they began to make merry.
And his elder son was out in the field. And as he was coming and drew near to the house, he heard the sound of rejoicing and merrymaking.
And he called one of the servants and asked him, "What is this?"
And he said to him, "Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fatted calf, because he has come back alive."
But he became angry and would not go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

And he answered and said to his father, "Look, all these years I have served you, and I never once disobeyed your command, and you never gave me even a single young goat so that I could make merry with my friends.
But when this son of yours came, who devoured your living with harlots, you killed the fatted calf for him."
And he said to him, "Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
But now it is right to make merry and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found."
And he said also to the disciples: "There was a certain rich man who had a steward. And charges were brought to him against this steward that he was squandering his goods.
And he called him and said to him, 'What is this that I hear about you? Give me an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward from now on.'
Then the steward said in his heart, 'What shall I do, since my lord is taking my stewardship away from me? I have no strength to work, and I am ashamed to beg.
I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, they will receive me into their houses.'
And he called each one of his lord's debtors, and said to the first, 'How much do you owe my lord?'
And he said, 'A hundred measures of oil.' And he said to him, 'Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty.'
Then he said to another, 'And how much do you owe?' And he said, 'A hundred measures of wheat.' He said to him also, 'Take your bill and write eighty.'
And the lord praised the steward of unrighteousness, because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this world are shrewder than the sons of light in their own generation.
And I say to you: make friends for yourselves by means of the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when you fail and depart from here, they may receive you into the eternal dwellings.
He who is faithful in little is faithful also in much; and he who is dishonest in little is dishonest also in much.
If, then, you have not been faithful with this mammon of unrighteousness, who will entrust to you the true riches?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?
No servant can serve two masters: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon."
The Pharisees also heard all these things, for they were lovers of money, and they scoffed at him.
And he said to them: "You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts [?]; for what is exalted among men is an abomination before God.
For the law and the prophets were until John; since then the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone is pressing into it by force.
It is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the law to fall.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and he who marries a woman divorced from her husband also commits adultery."
There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and made merry splendidly every day.
There was a certain poor man named Lazarus, who lay at his gate and was in misery.
And he longed to be filled with the crumbs that fell from that rich man's table; and even the dogs came and licked his sores.
And the poor man died, and he was carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
And in hell, being in torment, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
And he cried out and said: Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am tormented in this flame of fire.
But Abraham said to him: Son, remember that you received your good things in your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise evil things. And now, behold, he is comforted here, and you are tormented.
And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who wish to cross over from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross over from there to us.
Then he said: I beg you, father, send him to my father's house,
for I have five brothers, so that he may warn them, and they too may not come to this place of torment.
Abraham said to him: They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.
But he said: No, father Abraham; but if someone rises from the dead and goes to them, they will repent.
Abraham said to him: If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they believe even if someone rises from the dead.
Jesus said to his disciples: It is impossible that stumbling blocks should not come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
It would be better for him if a donkey's millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
So watch yourselves. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times turns back and says to you, 'I repent,' forgive him.
And the apostles said to the Lord: Increase our faith!
Jesus said to them: If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you could say to this sycamine tree, 'Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
Which of you, having a servant who is ploughing or tending sheep, would say to him at once when he comes in from the field, 'Come here and sit down'?
Would he not rather say to him, 'Prepare something for me to eat, and put on your belt and serve me while I eat and drink, and after that you may eat and drink too'?
Does he thank that servant because he did what he was commanded? I think not.
So you too, when you have done what you were commanded, say: 'We are worthless servants; we have done what we were obliged to do.'
And it happened that as he was going to Jerusalem, he was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
And as he entered a certain village, ten men with leprosy met him, and they stood at a distance.
And they raised their voices and said, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
And when he saw them, he said to them, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And as soon as they had gone from him, they were cleansed of their leprosy.
But one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back and glorified God with a loud voice.
And he fell down at the feet of Jesus and gave him thanks. And he was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered and said to him, "Were not all ten healed? And where are the nine?"
"Were none found to turn back and give glory to God, except only this foreigner?"
And he said to him, "Rise and go! Your faith has saved you."
The Pharisees asked him, "When will the kingdom of God come?" Jesus answered and said to them, "The kingdom of God will not come with observation;
nor will they say, 'Look, here it is!' or 'There!' For look, the kingdom of God is among you."
And he said to the disciples, "The days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
And they will say to you, 'Look, he is here!' and 'Look, he is there!' Do not go out, and do not follow them.
For as the lightning flashes from under one part of heaven and shines to under the other part of heaven, so will the Son of Man be in his days.
But first he must suffer much and be despised by this generation.
And as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man:
they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark. And the flood came and destroyed them all.
And likewise, as it was in the days of Lot: they were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building;
and on the day Lot went out of Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all.
So will it be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, whoever is on the roof, with his goods in the house, let him not come down to take them; and whoever is out in the field, let him not turn back again.
Remember Lot's wife.
Whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses it will save it.
I tell you, on that night there will be two in one bed: one will be taken, and the other will be left.
Two will be grinding together: one will be taken, and the other will be left."
And they answered and said to him, "Where, Lord?" And he said to them, "Wherever the body is, there the eagles will gather."
He also told them a parable, to show that they ought always to pray and not grow weary in prayer.
And he said: There was a certain judge in a city who did not fear God and was not ashamed before people.
And there was a certain widow in that same city. And she kept coming to him and saying to him: Give me justice against my adversary!
And for some time he would not listen to her. After this he said in his heart: Even though I do not fear God and am not ashamed before people,
because this widow keeps troubling me all the time, I will give her justice, so that she will not keep coming and wearing me out.
And the Lord said to them: Hear what the unjust judge says.
And will God not avenge his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night, and is he long-suffering toward them?
I tell you: he will avenge them quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?
He told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and despised others:
Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed this to himself: God, I thank you that I am not like other people, robbers, deceitful and adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week, and I offer a tithe of everything I acquire.
But the tax collector stood far off and did not dare even to lift up his eyes, but beat his breast and said: God, have mercy on me, a sinner.
I tell you: this man went down to his house justified rather than that Pharisee; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
They were bringing even little children to him, so that they might come near him. And when the disciples saw it, they tried to stop them.
But Jesus called them and said: Let these children come to me and do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Amen, I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it.
And a certain ruler asked him, saying: Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?
Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honour your father and your mother.
And he said: I have kept all these from my youth.
When Jesus heard this, he said to him: You still lack one thing: sell everything you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.
And when he heard this, he became sorrowful, for he was very rich.
When Jesus saw that he had become sorrowful, he said: How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a winch rope to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
But those who heard it said to him: Then who can be saved?
Jesus answered and said to them, "What is impossible for human beings is possible for God."
Peter said to him, "Look, we have left everything and followed you."
And Jesus said to them, "Amen, I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or father, or mother, or brothers, or wife, or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive many times as much in this present time, and in the age to come eternal life."
And he took the twelve aside and said to them, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
For he will be handed over to the Gentiles, and they will mock him, and insult him, and spit on him,
and they will torment him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise again."
But they understood none of these things; this saying was hidden from them, and they did not know what had been said.
And it happened that as they drew near to Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting by the road begging.
When he heard that a crowd was passing by, he asked, "What is this?"
They told him, "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by."
And he cried out and said, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Those who were walking in front rebuked him, telling him to be quiet. But he cried out all the more and said, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
And Jesus stopped and ordered him to be called. And when he came near, he asked him,
"What do you want me to do for you?" And he said to him, "Lord, let me receive my sight."
And Jesus said to him, "Receive your sight! Your faith has saved you."
And immediately he received his sight, and he followed him, glorifying God. And all the people saw it and praised God.
And he entered and was passing through Jericho.
And look, there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was very rich.
He wanted to see who Jesus was, but he could not see him because of the crowd, for he was short in stature.
So he ran on ahead and climbed up a sycamore tree to see him, because he was about to pass that way.
And when he came to that place, Jesus looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay in your house."
And he hurried and came down and brought him in with joy.
And all who saw it grumbled and said, "He has gone in to lodge with a sinful man."
Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord, I will give half of my goods to the poor; and if I have falsely accused anyone, I will pay him back fourfold."
Jesus said to him: "Today salvation has come to this house, for this man too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost."
And as the people were hearing this, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they supposed that the kingdom of God would appear immediately.
He said to them: "A certain nobleman went to a far country to receive a kingdom for himself and to return.
He called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas, and said to them: 'Trade with this until I come.'
But his citizens hated him, and they sent envoys after him and said to him: 'We do not want that man to reign over us.'
And when he returned, having received his kingdom, he ordered those servants to whom he had given the silver to be called, so that he might know what they had gained by trading.
The first came and said: 'Lord, your silver has gained ten more pounds.'
He said to him: 'Well done, good servant! Because you were faithful in a very little, have authority over ten cities.'
The second came and said: 'Lord, your silver has made five more pounds.'
He said to him also: 'And you, be over five cities.'
Then the third came and said: 'Lord, here is your silver, which I kept laid away in a cloth,
for I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man: you take up what you did not lay down, and you reap what you did not sow.'
He said to him: 'By your own mouth I will judge you, you wicked servant. You knew that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow.
Then why did you not put my silver in the bank, so that when I came I would have collected it with interest?'
And he said to those standing by: 'Take the silver from him and give it to the one who has ten pounds of silver.'
And they said to him: 'Lord, he has ten pounds.'
'I tell you that to everyone who has, more will be given; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slaughter them before me.'"
And when he had said this, he went on ahead of them, going up to Jerusalem.
And when he came near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of the disciples,
and said to them: "Go into the village ahead of you, and when you enter it you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it to me.
And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' say this: 'The Lord needs it.'"
So those who were sent went away and found it just as he had told them.
And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them: "Why are you untying that colt?"
And they said, "The Lord needs it."
And they brought it to Jesus, and they threw their garments on the colt, and Jesus sat on it.
And as he went in, they spread their garments on the road.
And as he drew near to the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began joyfully to praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen,
and they said, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!"
And some Pharisees from the crowd spoke to him and said, "Teacher, rebuke your disciples!"
But Jesus answered and said to them, "I tell you, if these were silent, the stones would cry out."
And as he drew near, he saw the city and wept over it,
and he said, "If only you had known on this day what makes for your peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
For the days will come upon you when your enemies' army will set up against you, and they will surround you and hem you in on every side,
and they will tear you down, and your children within you will fall, and not one stone will be left upon another within you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation."
And when he went into the temple, he began to drive out those who were selling and those who were buying,
and he said to them, "It is written: 'My house is a house of prayer,' but you have made it a den of robbers."
And he was there, teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the leaders of the people sought to destroy him,
and they could not find anything they might do to him, for all the people were devoted to listening to him.
And it happened in those days, while he was teaching the people and preaching the gospel in the temple, that the chief priests and the scribes came upon him together with the elders,
and they spoke to him and said, "Tell us, by what authority do you do this, or who gave you this authority?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "I too will ask you one question, and you tell me:
Was the baptism of John from heaven, or from men?"
And they deliberated with one another and said, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will say to us, 'Why did you not believe him?'
And if we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
And they answered and said, "We do not know where it was from."
And Jesus said to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do this."
And he began to tell them a parable: "A certain man planted a vineyard and gave it to tenant farmers, and went away for a long time.
And at the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants, so that they would give him some of the fruit. But the tenants beat him and tormented him and sent him away empty-handed.
And he sent another servant as well. But they beat him too and sent him away empty-handed.
Then he sent a third again. But they seized him, wounded him and threw him out.
And the lord of the vineyard said, "What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Who knows, perhaps they will respect him."
But when those tenant farmers saw him, they plotted among themselves and said, "This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, so that the inheritance may be ours."
And they took him outside the vineyard and killed him. Now what will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy those tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others." But when they heard this, they said, "May it never be!"
But he looked at them and said to them, "What then is this that is written: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone'?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces, and on whomever it falls, it will crush him."
And the chief priests and the scribes wanted to lay their hands on him at that very hour, but they feared the people, for they understood that he had told this parable against them.
And they watched him closely and sent spies, two-faced men who pretended to be righteous, so that they might catch him in some word and hand him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
And they questioned him, saying, "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and you show partiality to no one, but you truly teach the way of God.
Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?"
And when he perceived their cunning, he said to them, "Why are you testing me?
Show me a denarius." And they showed him one. And he said, "Whose image and inscription is this?" And they answered and said to him, "Caesar's."
And Jesus said to them, "Then give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
And they could find nothing in his words to use against him before the people. And they marveled at his answer and fell silent.
At that time some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is a resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying,
"Teacher, Moses wrote this for us: if someone's brother dies, having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers among us. And the first took a wife and died childless.
And the second and the third,
and they died childless. And likewise up to the seventh, and no child was left.
After all of them, the woman also died.
Now then, in the resurrection of the dead, whose wife will she be of them, since all seven had her as wife?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "The children of this world marry and are given in marriage.
But those who are made worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage,
Nor can death have power over them any longer, for they are equal to the angels, and they are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised, Moses also made known at the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
For he is not the God of the dead but of the living, for all are alive before him.
Some of the scribes answered and said to him: "Teacher, you have spoken well."
And from then on they no longer dared to question him. And the Lord said to them:
"How then do they say that the Christ is the son of David?
For David himself says in the Book of Psalms: 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool under your feet.'
David himself calls him Lord, so how is he his son?"
And as all the people were listening, he said to his disciples:
"Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes, and who love greetings in the streets, and the first seats in the synagogue, and the places of honor at meals,
who devour the houses of widows and, as a pretext, pray at great length. These will receive the greater condemnation."
And he looked up and saw the rich who were putting their offerings into the treasury.
And he saw a certain poor widow who put in two small coins (mites),
and he said: "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has offered more than all of them,
for all these put into this offering of God out of their abundance, but she, out of her want, offered all the living that she had."
And some were saying of the temple that it was built with fine and precious stones; and Jesus said:
"Do you see this? The days will come in which not one stone will be left upon another that will not be thrown down."
The disciples asked him: "Teacher, when then will this be, and what is the sign when this is about to take place?"
And he said: "Take heed that you are not led astray, for many will come in my name and say, 'I am he,' and, 'The time has come.' But do not go after them.
And when you hear of wars and tumults, do not be terrified, for this must take place first, but the end will not come at once."
Then he said to them: "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;
and there will be great earthquakes in various places, famines and pestilences; there will be terrors from heaven and great signs.

But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, and they will hand you over to synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors for my name's sake.
And this will turn out for you as a testimony.
Settle this in your hearts, that you do not prepare beforehand what answer you will give,
for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or answer.
For you will be handed over by fathers and mothers, and by brothers and friends and kinsmen, and they will put some of you to death.
And you will be hated by all for my name's sake.
And not a hair of your head will perish.
And by your endurance you will gain your souls.
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army of soldiers, then understand that its desolation has drawn near.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let those who are inside it get out; and let those who are in the country not enter there.
For these are days of vengeance, so that all the scriptures may be fulfilled.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days, for then there will be great distress upon the earth and wrath upon this people.
And they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led away captive by all the Gentiles; and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
And there will be signs in the sun and the moon and the stars, and on the earth distress [literally "a gathering"] of the nations, in bewilderment at the roaring of the sea and the shaking,
the spirits of men [?] from fear and from expectation of what is coming upon this world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with power and great glory.
And when all this begins to take place, lift up your eyes and raise your heads, for your redemption has drawn near.
And he told them a parable: Look at the fig tree and all the trees!
When they put forth leaves, you know for yourselves that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all this taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Amen, I say to you: this generation will not pass away until all this takes place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
Take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with revelry and drunkenness and the cares of this world, and that day come upon you suddenly,
for like a snare it will come upon those who dwell on the face of the whole earth.
Watch, therefore, at all times and pray, that you may be found worthy to escape all this that is going to take place, and to stand before the Son of Man.
And he himself was in the temple by day and taught; but at night he would go out and stay on the mount called the Mount of Olives.
And all the people would rise early in the morning and come to him in the temple to hear his words.
The feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called the Passover, was drawing near.
The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to kill him, but they were afraid of the people.
Then Satan entered into Judas, who was called Iscariot. He was one of the Twelve.
He went and spoke with the chief priests, the scribes and the leaders of the people about how he might hand him over to them.
They were glad and promised to give him silver.
He agreed with them, and he looked for a good time to hand him over to them away from the crowd.
The days of Unleavened Bread came, when the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
He sent Peter and John and said to them: "Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat it."
They said to him: "Where do you want us to prepare it for you?"
He said to them: "Look, as soon as you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him to the house that he enters.
Say to the master of the house: 'The Teacher says to you: Where is the guest room where I may eat this Passover with my disciples?'
He will show you a large upper room, already furnished. Make it ready for us there."
They went and found everything just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When the hour came, he sat down at the table, and the twelve apostles with him.
He said to them: "I have longed with all my heart to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
For I tell you, I will not eat it again from now on until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
He took a cup, gave thanks, and said: "Take this and share it among yourselves.
For I tell you, from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, gave it to them and said: "This is my body, given for you. Do this in remembrance of me."
In the same way he took the cup after supper and said: "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, poured out for you.
But look, the hand of the one who betrays me is with me on the table.
The Son of Man is going as it has been decreed for him, but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!"
They began to ask one another which of them it could be who was going to do this.
A dispute also arose among them about which of them should be considered the greatest.
He said to them: "The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called benefactors.
But you shall not be like that. Instead, let the greatest among you be like the youngest, and the leader like a servant.
Who is greater: the one who reclines at table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines at table? But I am among you as one who serves.
And you are the ones who have stood by me in my trials.
And I promise you the kingdom, as my Father promised it to me,
so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
And the Lord said: Simon, Simon, look: the devil has demanded to have you, to sift you like wheat.
But I have pleaded with my Father for you, that your faith may not fail. And when you have once turned back, strengthen your brothers.
But he said: Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death.
But he said: I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today before you have denied three times that you know me.
And he said to them: When I sent you out without purse, bag, or sandals, did you lack anything? And they said: We lacked nothing.
And then he said to them: But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a bag too; and whoever does not have one, let him sell his garment and buy a sword.
I tell you: this scripture must still be fulfilled in me: 'He was counted among the lawless.' For what concerns me is coming to its end.
And they said to him: Lord, look, here are two knives. And he said to them: It is enough.
And he went out from there and went, as was his custom, to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples also followed him.
And when he came to the place, he said to them: Pray that you may not enter into temptation.
And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw, knelt down, and prayed.
And he said: Father, if you are willing, let this cup pass from me. Yet not my will, but let your will be done!
And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
And he was in agony, and he prayed all the more. And his sweat became like drops of blood falling down on the ground.
And he rose from prayer and came to his disciples, and found them asleep from grief.
And he said to them: Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation.

And while he was still saying this, look, a crowd came, and the man called Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, was leading them. He came near to Jesus to kiss him, for he had given them this sign, saying: The one I kiss is the man.
But Jesus said to him: Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?
When those who were with him saw what was happening, they said to him: Lord, shall we strike them down with the sword?
And one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
Jesus answered and said to them, "Let it go this far!" And he touched his ear and healed him.
Jesus said to those who had come against him, the chief priests, the captains of the temple and the elders: "You have come out with swords and clubs as if against a robber.
Day after day I was with you in the temple, and you did not lay a hand on me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness."
When they had seized him, they led him away and brought him into the house of the high priest. Peter followed at a distance.
They lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down around it, and Peter also sat among them.
A certain maidservant saw him sitting in the light. She looked closely at him and said, "This man was with him too."
But he denied it and said, "Woman, I do not know him."
A little later someone else saw him and said, "You are one of them too." But Peter said, "Man, I am not one of them."
About an hour later someone else insisted, saying, "This man was certainly with him too, for he is a Galilean."
But Peter said to him, "Man, I do not know what you are saying." At once, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said to him, "Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times."
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
The men who had seized Jesus mocked him and beat him.
They covered his head, struck him on the face and questioned him, saying, "Prophesy! Who is it that struck you?"
And they said many other blasphemous things against him.
When day dawned, the elders of the people, the chief priests and the scribes gathered together and brought him up to their council,
and they said to him, "If you are the Christ, tell us!" Jesus said to them, "If I tell you, you will not believe me;
and if I ask you, you will not answer me or release me.
From now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
They all said to him, "Are you the Son of God, then?" Jesus said to them, "You say that I am."
And they said, "Why do we still need witnesses? We have heard it ourselves from his own mouth."
Then their whole crowd rose up and brought him to Pilate.
They began to accuse him, saying, "We found this man leading our nation astray, forbidding the payment of tribute to Caesar, and calling himself Christ and king."
Pilate questioned him and said to him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" He said to him, "You say so."
Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the people, "I find no guilt in this man."
But they grew all the more insistent and said, "He stirs up the people and teaches throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place."
When Pilate heard "Galilee," he asked them whether this man was from Galilee.
And when he understood that he was under Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, for Herod too was in Jerusalem at that time, in those days.
When Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had been hearing about him and longed to see some sign performed by him.
And he questioned him at length, but he himself gave him no answer at all.
The chief priests and the scribes stood there and vehemently accused him.
And Herod, with his soldiers, treated him with contempt; they mocked him, dressed him in a shining robe, and sent him back to Pilate.
And Pilate and Herod became friends with each other on that day, for before this they had been enemies.
Then Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers and the people,
and said to them, "You brought me this man as one who leads the people astray, and I examined him in your presence and found no guilt in this man regarding the things you accuse him of.
Neither did Herod, for I sent him to him, and look, he has done nothing deserving death.
I will therefore punish him and release him."
For he was obliged to release one man to them at the feast.
The whole crowd cried out together, saying, "Take this man away and release Barabbas to us!"
He had been thrown into prison for a riot in the city and for murder.
Pilate called to them again, because he wanted to release Jesus.
But they kept shouting, "Crucify him, crucify him!"
A third time he said to them, "What evil has this man done? I have found in him no guilt deserving death. I will therefore punish him and release him."
But they pressed him with loud voices, demanding that he be crucified. And their voices, and those of the chief priests, prevailed.
Then Pilate decided that their demand should be granted,
and he released to them Barabbas, the man who had been thrown into prison for riot and murder, the one they asked for; but Jesus he handed over to their will.
As they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, and laid the cross on him, and he carried it behind Jesus.
A great crowd of people followed him, including women who were beating their breasts and weeping for him.
Jesus turned to them and said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
For behold, the days are coming when they will say, 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.'
Then they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us!' and to the hills, 'Cover us!'
For if they do this to the green tree, what will happen to the dry?
Then they were also leading two others, evildoers, to be put to death with him.
And when they had brought him to the place called the Place of the Skull, there they crucified him, and the evildoers with him; they crucified one on his right and one on his left.
And Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." And as they were dividing his clothing, they cast lots.
And the people stood and watched. And the rulers with them also mocked him, saying, "He saved others; let him save himself too, if he is the Christ, the Chosen One of God."
The soldiers also mocked him, coming up to him and offering him vinegar,
and saying to him, "If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!"
There was also an inscription, written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew letters: "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."
And one of the evildoers who were hanging there reviled him, saying to him, "If you are the Christ, save yourself and us too!"
The other companion answered, rebuked him and said to him, "Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same sentence?
And we justly receive what is deserved for what we have done, but this man has done nothing wrong."
And he said to Jesus, "Remember me, Lord, when you come in your kingdom."
And Jesus said to him, "Amen, I say to you: today you will be with me in Paradise."
And it was the sixth hour, and there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
And the sun was darkened, and the curtain of the temple was torn down the middle.
And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said, "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit." And having said this, he gave up his spirit.
And when the centurion saw this thing, he glorified God and said, "Truly this man was righteous."
And all who had come there with them, who had seen this sight and these things, beat their breasts and went away.
And all his acquaintances stood at a distance; and the women who had followed him from Galilee were watching him.
And behold, there was a man named Joseph, a member of the council, a good and righteous man;
he had not agreed with their counsel and their deed. He was from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, and he too was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus,
and he took it down and wrapped it in a linen shroud, and laid it in a tomb hewn out of rock, where no one had yet been laid.
And that day was the Day of Preparation (Friday), and the Sabbath was dawning.
The women who had come with him from Galilee also followed, and they saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
And they went and prepared fragrant spices and ointment, and on the Sabbath they rested, according to the commandment.
But on the first day of the week, very early at dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the fragrant spices and ointment they had prepared, and some others were with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
And when they went inside, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
And while they were perplexed about this, behold, two men in shining garments stood over them.
And as they were frightened and bowed their faces to the ground, the men said to them: "Why do you seek the living one among the dead?
He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee,
and said: 'The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise.'"
And they remembered his words.
And they returned from the tomb and told all this to the eleven and to all the others.
Now it was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.
And their words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe them.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb, and he looked into the tomb and saw only the linen cloths lying there. And he went away by himself, amazed at what had happened.
And behold, that same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, which is sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
And they were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
And while they were talking and discussing, Jesus himself came near to them and walked along with them.
But their eyes were held, so that they could not recognize him.
And he said to them: "What are these words that you are exchanging with each other as you walk, and why are you sad?"
One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said to him: "Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who does not know what has happened there in these days?"
And he said to them: "What things?" And they said to him: "About Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet, mighty in deed and in his word before God and all the people;
how the chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death, and crucified him.
But we had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, today is the third day since these things happened.
Moreover, some women of our group amazed us: they went to the tomb at dawn
and did not find his body. They came and said that they had even seen a vision of angels, who told them that he is alive.
And some of those who were with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but him they did not see.
And he said to them: O you ignorant ones, slow of heart to believe all that the prophets spoke!
Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?
And beginning from Moses and the prophets, he interpreted to them the things concerning himself in all the scriptures.
And they drew near to the village to which they were going. But he made as though he would go farther.
But they urged him, saying to him: Stay with us, for it is evening, and the day is now far spent. And he went in to stay with them.
And it came to pass, as he reclined at table with them, that he took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them.
Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him. And he vanished from their sight.
And they said to one another: Were not our hearts burning within us while he was speaking to us on the road and while he was interpreting the scriptures to us?
And they rose up that same hour and returned to Jerusalem, and they found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
who were saying: The Lord has truly risen and has appeared to Simon.
And they told what had happened on the road, and how he had been made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
And while they were still saying this, Jesus himself stood in their midst and said to them: Peace be with you!
But they were startled and frightened, and thought that they were seeing a spirit.
And he said to them: Why are you troubled, and why do many thoughts arise in your hearts?
See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself. Touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.
And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
And while they still did not believe for joy and were marvelling, Jesus said to them: Do you have anything here to eat?
And they gave him a piece of broiled fish and a honeycomb.
And he ate in their presence, and took what was left and gave it to them,
and said: These are the words that I spoke to you while I was still with you: that everything written about me in the law of Moses, in the prophets, and in the psalms must be fulfilled.
Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures,
and said to them: Thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day,
and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations. Begin from Jerusalem,
for you are witnesses of all these things.
And behold, I will send you the promise of my Father. But you stay here in this city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.
And he led them out as far as Bethany, raised his hands and blessed them.
And as Jesus was blessing them, he parted from them and was going up into heaven.
And they worshipped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
And they were always in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
